Complexification and extrapolation is a technique for accelerating convergence in iterative methods for electromagnetic scattering problems.
The method is based on the principle of limiting absorption.
Complexification involves introducing an imaginary part to the wavenumber and extrapolating solutions back to the real axis.
The technique is particularly effective for second-kind integral equations (SKIEs).
Complexification reduces the condition number of the discrete matrix by 4 or 5 orders of magnitude.
The fast multipole method (FMM) is used as the platform for exploring complexification.
